latest_release.body:
### Fixed

- Resume a live eval comparison after returning to the tab when its last poll failed, while keeping normal focus reads disabled.

- Keep live Project mounts reachable on isolated production Compose hosts with an opt-in supervisor-only gateway bridge. Deployment refuses incomplete filesystem configuration without placing sandboxd on the proxy network or changing agent networking.

- Remove an agent’s own environment guards before its suites, so deleting a guarded agent does not depend on PostgreSQL cascade ordering. Other agents’ guards and suite deletion protections stay in place.

- A failed background job keeps only messages AgenticOS wrote as its last error. Another exception names its type, and its message stays in the worker log.
- A manual eval checks before every case that its starter may still run the agent and the dataset.
- Keep an Improve variant search going when a round of proposals is refused or unanswered: it is asked again up to three times, and a scoring answer the provider could not give counts as ungraded instead of failing the search.
- Fail a skill Improve session's step that is refused, with its reason and a Retry, instead of leaving the session stuck; a step past the spending limit stops on its budget.
- Parse dataset imports off the event loop, a row at a time, so a large or deeply nested file cannot stall the API.
- Keep a regression a finished skill check stage confirmed when another stage of the agent could not finish, and say so on the agent's row.
- Keep an Improve search's units in step with their job and budget: the Try again note reaches the helper, an answer's cap covers longer instructions and agents whose answers cost nothing, and a unit that runs out of time keeps its answers.
- Name a skill's test set apart from a dataset that already holds its name, discard a check and its proposal without deadlocking, and move a skill check on when its stage run is cancelled, reaped or lost.
- Admit a later Improve attempt on its own training questions, list every open session and every knowledge topic a session found to the Architect, and learn only from answers the agent itself gave.
- Correct the eval write-tool table, the authoring assistant's access and tools, and what a skill session's readers see in the documentation.
- Keep Improve session pages loading while permissions are read, with a retry when they cannot be, instead of saying access is missing. Stop polling live pages after a failed read, say which part stopped updating with a Retry, and keep a loaded eval result on screen when a refresh fails. A link to a dataset case says the case is gone only when it is.
- Show a skill merge's candidate text as source, open each changed file to what each side changed (or offer each side as a download), and say how many cited evidence items come from agents the reader cannot see.
- Give keyboard focus back to where it was when a dialog opened without a trigger closes. Name the verdict in the attempt picker and the state of each skill check row for screen readers. Offer "See what changed" for a tested draft only with edit access, and say when History cannot read the tested version.
- Name every reason an agent goes unchecked in a skill check's price, and list regressions first among changed answers with a count of those left out. Count a session's knowledge topics by their own ids, with a retry when they cannot be read. Read and name a dataset linked into the Improve start dialog before pricing on it.

### Changed

- The judge prompt fences the case and the answer and ends on the rule that they are data; its version moves to 5. Scores graded with the earlier prompt are no longer reused as cached baselines or compared with new ones, so the first eval run or Improve session after the upgrade grades its answers from scratch, and grading an older eval score again asks to run the eval again.
- Secret redaction recognises more shapes: passwords in URLs, keys in query strings and form bodies, Basic and

detail.readme:
Open-source, self-hosted AI agent platform for your company's AI teammates.
Build, run and govern agents on your own servers and models: shared chat, RAG, skills, a real browser, MCP, budgets, approvals and an audit trail.
Apache-2.0 · built on Pydantic AI

🏆 Built by Vstorm — a recipient of the 2026 Open Agentic AI Innovation Award.
Recognized by the Agentic AI Foundation for adopting AGENTS.md and integrating MCP in its open-source framework.
Read the AAIF announcement · The work behind the award

See it · Highlights · What is it? · Quick start · Server, desktop & mobile · Integrations · Product tour · Find your path · What ships · FAQ · Website · Introduction deck · Documentation

English · Polski · Deutsch · Español

*Prepared conversation with fictional sales data in the real Visuals renderer. No live CRM or new model-generation run is represented.* AgenticOS gives every team AI teammates: agents that work with files, run code, browse the web and use your company's tools and knowledge. Your colleagues and your agents work in the same live chat, and any agent can hand code to Claude Code or Codex, on the ChatGPT or Claude subscription you already pay for. It is open source (Apache-2.0) and self-hosted, a layer you run on your own infrastructure. Build and publish agents in the browser, share them with colleagues, and manage their access, cost and results in one place. **New here?** Click through the [17-slide introduction](https://vstorm-co.github.io/agenticos/presentation/): the problem, the idea, the product on real screens, its controls and limits, and how to start. For every screen in detail, open the [47-slide product tour](https://vstorm-co.github.io/agenticos/presentation/tour/). Arrow keys step through either deck; `O` lists every slide. ## New in the latest releases - **Your local Claude Code or Codex, inside desktop chat.** Choose a coding agent per conversation, work in an approved local folder, resume its session and apply corrections while it works. Sign in through the coding agent's own terminal flow. - **Your skills and project instructions.** Opt a desktop conversation into local skills and `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md`, read from your computer. Each new chat starts with this sharing off. - **Discord joins Slack, Teams, Telegram and Mattermost.** Answer mentions, direct messages and `/ask`; review approvals and questions in the channel. [Set up a channel](https://vstorm-co.github.io/agenticos/channels/). - **More useful Visuals and Apps.** Draw country maps, pins and routes with the bundled `AOWorldMap`, or use the presentation skills to build a deck as an App. A command watcher can follow test or log output while an agent works. [Release notes](https://github.com/vstorm-co/agenticos/releases) · [Desktop guide](https://vstorm-co.github.io/agenticos/desktop/) ## ⚡ Highlights ### Your team and your agents, in one live room A project gives everyone the same files, instructions and a computer for the agents. Invite colleagues and work the way a team works: see who is here, watch a teammate's agent answer as it is written, and bring in any agent, tool or document with an `@`. ### Reply to anyone, and the agent knows who said what Reply to a person or an agent's answer, and the agent applies the change and says whose it was. Every message carries a name, so a decision has an owner. ### Claude Code and Codex, on your team Any agent can hand software work to Claude Code or Codex. They build in the agent's own computer, on your ChatGPT or Claude subscription, and report what they changed, what they checked and what they need from you. *Prepared interface example: Claude Code implements a supplier portal and Codex reviews it in read-only mode. Fictional handoffs; no coding CLI execution is represented.* ### Ask how it works, get a drawing you can use An agent draws while it writes: a diagram from your documents, a calculator with sliders, a chart or a 3D scene, live under its message. One click saves it as an app your team opens by link. *A prepared manufacturing Visual inside chat: a supply network, inbound delivery exceptions and assembly windows. Interactive fictional data; no ERP, machine connection or live model call is represented.* ### Write to an agent and leave Ask for research that takes a while and close the tab. The agent keeps working, the answer lands in the conversation, and the bell tells you it is done. ### Your day, on one screen Open the console to what your agents did, the calls waiting on you and the conversations to pick up again - with a tour of what they can do that is easy to miss. ### Agents that work as a team A lead agent hands parts of a task to colleagues and writes up what they found - you see who it asked, and what each said. ### A real browser, right in the chat Watch it click through sites, take over when a sign-in needs you, point at a spot to comment. ### Build, equip and test in one window Enable tools and try a real task in the draft test panel before publishing the agent for colleagues. ### Apps, not just answers An agent publishes a dashboard or a report as a page with a stable link and versions. *Northline: a prepared supply and production planning App with fictional shipments, local delay simulation and assembly windows.*
More prepared Apps: motor assembly and sales intelligence Working local demonstrations with fictional data. Motor Atlas lets you inspect a conceptual assembly and its component records; Revenue Pulse recalculates sales metrics by region and period. No equipment, ERP or CRM is connected.
### A website widget, on your own site The actual AgenticOS widget runs a published, read-only agent on the fictional Trail Supply website. In the recorded local test it answered using the seeded catalog in its instructions. Live inventory, purchases and payments are not connected. [Build and publish a website widget](https://vstorm-co.github.io/agenticos/howto/support-widget/) ### 4,700+ MCP servers Connect Notion, GitHub, Jira or your own server, and choose which tools each agent may call. ### Work in AgenticOS from Claude Code, Codex or Cursor AgenticOS is an MCP server. Add it with one command and sign in through the browser: your coding assistant can list and run agents, read runs and what they cost, and search and fill knowledge bases, within what you allowed. ## 📸 See it in action Browse the [current product gallery](https://vstorm-co.github.io/agenticos/screens/). Motor Atlas below is a prepared, interactive assembly explorer with fictional component records and telemetry; it is not a CAD drawing. ## 🧩 Build useful work around your agents Use [Workflows](https://vstorm-co.github.io/agenticos/workflows/) to connect typed steps, agent calls and MCP tools on a visual canvas. Store structured results in [Virtual Tables](https://vstorm-co.github.io/agenticos/virtual-tables/), start work with [Routines](https://vstorm-co.github.io/agenticos/triggers/), and review runs and approvals. [Voice calls](https://vstorm-co.github.io/agenticos/voice/) and the [desktop app](https://vstorm-co.github.io/agenticos/desktop/) provide other ways to work with the same published agents. **Visual workflows, from lead intake to a human-reviewed handoff.** Illustrative 30-step draft with Google Workspace, Microsoft 365, HubSpot, Salesforce, Notion, Slack, agents and approvals. Connections are demo placeholders; this is not an executed integration. **Structured work your agents and your team can read together.** Virtual Tables with fictional companies, typed fields, stages and next actions. Switch between a grid and a kanban board. Start with a recognizable task: an [LLM wiki in a Project](https://vstorm-co.github.io/agenticos/projects/), a [website agent widget](https://vstorm-co.github.io/agenticos/channels/), or a team working from shared project files and instructions. A widget supplies the conversation surface; recommendations and cart actions still need your catalog, tool integration and permission checks. ## 💡 What is AgenticOS? **AgenticOS is an open-source (Apache-2.0), self-hosted layer for building, sharing and governing AI agents across a company.** Teams configure an agent in the browser by writing its instructions, choosing a model and switching on tools. They connect it to company documents and apps, and publish it to web chat, Slack, Teams, Discord, Mattermost, Telegram, a website widget or an API. Administrators control who can use each agent, what it may spend and which actions need a person's approval. Every run is recorded. Most agent frameworks give you a library, so every change to an agent's behaviour is a pull request, a review and a release. That is the wrong shape for the small agents a company actually wants, because the person who knows what the agent should say is not the person with commit access. **Code defines, configuration composes:** engineers extend what there is to assemble, and configuration can only ever reach what code registered. It runs on your own infrastructure with Docker Compose and works with 28 model providers, including your ChatGPT subscription and local models through Ollama and vLLM. Agents run on [Pydantic AI](https://ai.pydantic.dev) and [pydantic-ai-harness](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/harness/); the layer around them uses FastAPI, PostgreSQL with pgvector and Next.js. It is maintained by [Vstorm](https://vstorm.co). **Who it is for:** - Companies that want **an internal AI agent layer** they own, instead of per-seat assistants in a vendor's cloud. - Teams with **repeated work over documents and tools**, such as reports, support answers, contract checks and data analysis. - IT and security teams that need **data sovereignty, company sign-in, budgets, approvals and an audit trail** for AI agents. - Engineers who want **typed Python extension points** and a console their non-technical colleagues can use.

How it fits into your company. Illustrated people; the agents are examples.

**How AgenticOS fits into a company:** departments such as finance, operations or the board use shared agents in web chat, Slack or a private workspace. Your systems call agents through the API, and events or schedules start them automatically. Every request passes the same controls: roles, budgets, approvals, guardrails and a recorded run. Your data, vectors, code sandboxes, the credential vault and optional local models stay on your infrastructure. Hosted models, SaaS tools and document sources outside are used only when you configure them. 28 model providers · 4,700+ MCP gallery entries · shared chat and Projects · visual workflows and virtual tables · web, desktop, API and messaging channels. Configure availability and tools for each published agent. ## ✨ What you can do | For your team | What AgenticOS provides | |---|---| | [Work with files and code](#-work-with-files-and-code) | Analyze CSVs, produce charts and documents, work on repositories | | [Build reusable agents](#-build-agents-your-team-can-reuse) | Choose models and tools, publish versions, share agents with colleagues | | [Connect company knowledge](#-teach-agents-how-your-team-works) | Reuse skills, context and searchable documents across agents | | [Share the results](#-publish-results-as-interactive-pages) | Publish interactive pages with stable links and version history | | [Run and monitor](#-track-runs-costs-and-approvals) | Customize dashboards, inspect runs, schedule tasks and set budgets | | [Organize company access](#-organize-teams-with-roles-and-groups) | Combine roles, department groups and company sign-in | ## 🚀 Quick start ### Choose how you want to start **One company workspace, many ways to connect.** The server runs AgenticOS; the desktop app connects to it. Joining an existing workspace needs no Docker or developer tools. | Your situation | Next step | |---|---| | Your company already has AgenticOS | Ask for the workspace URL and sign in through your browser, or [install the desktop app](#install-the-desktop-app). | | You want a workspace for your company | Have your IT team [deploy a server](#deploy-a-company-server), or [ask Vstorm to help](https://vstorm.co/contact-us/). | | You want to try it on your computer without terminal commands | [Install the desktop app](#install-the-desktop-app), choose **On this computer** and follow setup. Review the [requirements](https://vstorm-co.github.io/agenticos/desktop/#running-it) first; AI requires a configured model, while recorded examples need none. | | You are a developer exploring locally | [Run the Docker quickstart](#try-it-locally). | ### Try it locally
For developers: try AgenticOS locally with Docker Start with Docker Compose and access to a model provider. On macOS or Linux, run: ```bash curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vstorm-co/agenticos/main/scripts/quickstart.sh | bash ``` On Windows, run the same command inside WSL2 with Docker Desktop's WSL2 integration switched on. The installer asks for a model provider and key, your login and an organization name, pulls the published images and starts a deployment with a working agent in it. A host with 4 vCPU and 8 GB of RAM runs it. Then open **http://localhost:3000** and sign in with the login you chose during installation. **Your first agent:** follow the [document-assistant walkthrough](https://vstorm-co.github.io/agenticos/howto/first-document-agent/) to upload a handbook, ask questions and check answers against cited sources. Then pick a next task from [30 tutorials](https://vstorm-co.github.io/agenticos/use-cases/), each with a sample input and a check you can run.
Inspect the installer or deploy another way Read the [installer](scripts/quickstart.sh) before running it. To check prerequisites without installing: ```bash curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vstorm-co/agenticos/main/scripts/quickstart.sh | bash -s -- --check ``` For manual Docker Compose setup, pinned versions and troubleshooting, follow the [installation guide](https://vstorm-co.github.io/agenticos/install/). For development from source, see [Contributing](https://vstorm-co.github.io/agenticos/help/).
## ☁️ One-click deploy Review the provider's instructions, image versions and included services before deploying. These hosting templates are maintained separately from this repository. The Railway template currently pins an older AgenticOS release and does not include the local code sandbox. ## Run on your server. Open it anywhere. The server holds the workspace. The browser, desktop app and phone connect to that deployment with its accounts, agents and access controls. ### Deploy a company server Your IT team sets up the workspace once, then shares an HTTPS address and creates your account. You can use that address in a browser or in the desktop app. For an assisted rollout, [talk to Vstorm](https://vstorm.co/contact-us/).
Server setup for IT and developers Use a Linux host with **4 vCPU and 8 GB RAM**, Docker Engine 24+, Compose 2.24+ and `make`. Point two DNS names at it — for example `app.example.com` and `api.example.com` — and allow HTTPS through a reverse proxy. The supported deployment is Docker Compose on one host. ```bash # On the server. Start from a released version so code and images stay aligned. git clone --branch v1.38.2 --depth 1 https://github.com/vstorm-co/agenticos.git cd agenticos bash scripts/server-init.sh ``` The setup asks for the site/API hostnames and certificate email, then generates `backend/.env`. Set `AGENTICOS_VERSION=1.38.2` there to pin this release. For a new host using the bundled Traefik proxy: ```bash docker network create traefik_webgateway docker compose --env-file backend/.env -f docker-compose-traefik.yml up -d make prod PROXY=traefik make prod-frontend PROXY=traefik ``` Then [bootstrap the first organization, owner and agent](https://vstorm-co.github.io/agenticos/deploy/#start-it-and-create-the-first-account), open your site's HTTPS address and add your organization's model credentials. The guide also covers an existing proxy, Nginx, updates and backups. Keep a backup of the database **and the vault key in `backend/.env`**. ```bash docker compose --env-file backend/.env -f docker-compose-prod.yml \ exec -T app agenticos cmd bootstrap \ --email you@example.com --password '' \ --org 'Your Company' --provider anthropic --api-key '' ``` [Complete server deployment guide](https://vstorm-co.github.io/agenticos/deploy/) · [Configuration checklist](https://vstorm-co.github.io/agenticos/configuration/#production-checklist)
### Install the desktop app Download an installer from [release v1.38.2](https://github.com/vstorm-co/agenticos/releases/tag/v1.38.2): | System | Download v1.38.2 | What to do | |---|---|---| | **macOS** | [Apple silicon · DMG](https://github.com/vstorm-co/agenticos/releases/download/v1.38.2/AgenticOS_1.38.2_aarch64.dmg) · [Intel · DMG](https://github.com/vstorm-co/agenticos/releases/download/v1.38.2/AgenticOS_1.38.2_x64.dmg) | Open the DMG and drag AgenticOS into Applications. | | **Windows x64** | [EXE](https://github.com/vstorm-co/agenticos/releases/download/v1.38.2/AgenticOS_1.38.2_x64-setup.exe) · [MSI](https://github.com/vstorm-co/agenticos/releases/download/v1.38.2/AgenticOS_1.38.2_x64_en-US.msi) | Open the EXE and follow the installer. MSI is for managed IT deployment. | | **Linux x64** | [DEB](https://github.com/vstorm-co/agenticos/releases/download/v1.38.2/AgenticOS_1.38.2_amd64.deb) · [RPM](https://github.com/vstorm-co/agenticos/releases/download/v1.38.2/AgenticOS-1.38.2-1.x86_64.rpm) · [AppImage](https://github.com/vstorm-co/agenticos/releases/download/v1.38.2/AgenticOS_1.38.2_amd64.AppImage) | Open DEB/RPM in your software installer. For AppImage, allow execution in file properties. | On a Mac, choose **Apple menu → About This Mac**: “Chip” identifies Apple silicon; “Processor: Intel” identifies an Intel Mac. **Prefer Homebrew on macOS?** The project’s [Homebrew tap](https://github.com/vstorm-co/homebrew-agenticos) chooses the correct Mac installer. Its cask clears the download quarantine flag for AgenticOS; it does not provide Apple notarization: ```bash brew install --cask vstorm-co/agenticos/agenticos ``` **After installing:** open AgenticOS, enter the HTTPS workspace address your team gave you and sign in. Connecting to an existing server needs no local Docker. To create a local workspace instead, choose the local-instance option in the wizard; that needs Docker. On macOS, builds are not Apple-notarized; a browser-downloaded DMG may need **System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway**. See the [installation guide](https://vstorm-co.github.io/agenticos/desktop/#installing-the-app). Beyond the console, desktop adds Quick Ask, local files and computer access with your consent, and local Claude Code / Codex. Under **Settings → Desktop app**, check the installed coding agents and sign in through their terminal. Choose one in **Chat controls**, grant a working folder full access and confirm the task in the native dialog. **My skills and instructions** is a separate, optional choice for each chat. [Desktop setup and local agents](https://vstorm-co.github.io/agenticos/desktop/) ### Use AgenticOS on your phone **Available now without a build:** open your deployment's HTTPS address in a mobile browser and sign in. Use the install prompt on a supported browser; on iPhone, choose **Share → Add to Home Screen**. The console adapts to a phone, including chat, files and approvals. **Native iOS and Android:** the source is included in `mobile/`, with biometric locking, sharing, widgets and native notification integrations. These are currently **development builds**, with no public App Store, Google Play, TestFlight or supported release download. To try the native app, install Rust plus Xcode on macOS (iOS), or the Android SDK/NDK and JDK (Android), then: ```bash cd mobile bun install --frozen-lockfile bun run ios # iOS development on macOS # or: bun run android ``` Install with your own platform signing/provisioning where required. Enter a server address reachable from the phone, or pair from **Settings → Mobile app** using the one-time QR code and confirm the account. `localhost` on a phone refers to the phone itself. Native push needs the deployment's platform-specific configuration; the [mobile guide](https://vstorm-co.github.io/agenticos/mobile/) covers build prerequisites, pairing and notifications. ## 🔌 Connect the apps your team already uses AgenticOS connects agents to the models, chat tools, business apps and document stores a company already uses, so an agent can read a Notion brief, search SharePoint documents or answer in Slack under the same access rules and budget. | Connect | How | Read | |---|---|---| | **Chat tools** | Publish an agent to Slack, Mattermost or Telegram, a website widget, a hosted page, the API or a WebSocket | [Channels](https://vstorm-co.github.io/agenticos/channels/) | | **Business tools** | **4,700+ MCP servers** in the gallery (Notion, GitHub, Jira, HubSpot, Stripe…) and your own servers; choose which tools each agent may call | [MCP](https://vstorm-co.github.io/agenticos/mcp/) | | **Documents** | Sync Google Drive, S3/MinIO, Git repositories, websites, SharePoint and OneDrive into knowledge bases | [Sync sources](https://vstorm-co.github.io/agenticos/howto/configure-sync-sources/) | | **Events** | Start agents on a schedule, a new GitHub issue, a Gmail message or a signed webhook | [Routines](https://vstorm-co.github.io/agenticos/triggers/) | | **Models** | 28 providers, your ChatGPT subscription, your cloud contract (Azure, Bedrock, Vertex) or local models (Ollama, vLLM) | [Models](https://vstorm-co.github.io/agenticos/models/) | Registry listings are publisher-provided metadata; each connection needs its own setup and access review. Outlook email and calendar connect through a third-party MCP service. Logos identify connection options and do not imply a partnership. ## 🧩 Build, share and operate ### 🤖 Build agents your team can reuse Choose an agent's model, instructions and tools in the browser. Publish a version for colleagues to use; inspect earlier versions and roll back when needed. Keep specialized agents for research, reporting, coding or operations in one catalog. The agent builder has four areas: **(1)** the name and publishing status, where a draft stays private until you publish a version; **(2)** tabs for the toolbox, MCP servers, limits, availability and version history; **(3)** the instructions, written in plain language like a brief for a new colleague; and **(4)** the model, chosen per agent from your configured providers. Colleagues can use a published agent in **web chat, Slack, Mattermost or Telegram** when those channels are configured, on a **website widget** or a **hosted page**, or through the **API** and **WebSocket**. [Build an agent](https://vstorm-co.github.io/agenticos/first-agent/) · [Connect a channel](https://vstorm-co.github.io/agenticos/channels/) ### 📂 Work with files and code Ask an agent to analyze a spreadsheet, produce a chart, prepare a document or work on a repository. With a container-backed sandbox configured and command execution enabled, it can **read and edit files, run shell commands, and execute Python or JavaScript**. The bundled workbench includes data, charting and document tools, including LibreOffice. If you use [Claude Code](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/overview) or [Codex](https://developers.openai.com/codex/cli/), the file-and-command workflow will feel familiar. AgenticOS brings that kind of work into a shared, self-hosted layer with company knowledge, reusable agents and organization access controls. What an agent can accomplish depends on its model, enabled tools and instructions. [Sandbox configuration](https://vstorm-co.github.io/agenticos/sandbox/) ### 🧠 Teach agents how your team works - **Skills** hold reusable procedures: how to review code, write a report or research a market. Maintain them once and reuse them across agents. - **Context** holds standing knowledge such as a glossary, policy or brand voice. Include it in the prompt or let the agent read it on demand. - **Knowledge bases (RAG)** make uploaded documents searchable. Choose parsing options, inspect processing status and chunks, or sync them from a source listed below. **How retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) works in AgenticOS:** documents are uploaded or synced from Google Drive, S3/MinIO, Git, websites, SharePoint or OneDrive. They are read by a parser: PyMuPDF and LiteParse run locally, with OCR for scans, while LlamaParse is a cloud service. Documents are then split into chunks, embedded with an OpenAI, OpenRouter or local Ollama model, and stored in PostgreSQL with pgvector. At question time the agent searches the vectors with filters and answers with citations. [Skills](https://vstorm-co.github.io/agenticos/skills/) · [Context](https://vstorm-co.github.io/agenticos/context/) · [Document processing](https://vstorm-co.github.io/agenticos/file-processing/) · [Sync sources](https://vstorm-co.github.io/agenticos/howto/configure-sync-sources/) ### 🎨 Publish results as interactive pages Agents can publish reports, interactive comparisons and small dashboards as **apps**. Choose who can open them; updates keep the same link and earlier versions remain readable. Public links can expire, require a password or restrict which sites may embed them. [Share an app](https://vstorm-co.github.io/agenticos/artifacts/) ### 📊 Track runs, costs and approvals The dashboard answers six questions for a chosen period: how many runs there were, how many finished, what they cost and how many people used agents; how runs changed over time; what failed, waited for approval or was stopped by a budget; where runs came from; and which agents people actually use. Customize the **dashboard** around your work. **Activity** lets you inspect runs and tool calls, compare agent versions and export records. **Budgets** per agent and organization are checked before each model request. **Approval policies** make sensitive tools wait for a person, and **routines** repeat work on schedules or events such as a new GitHub issue, a Gmail message or a signed webhook. [Run history, budgets and approvals](https://vstorm-co.github.io/agenticos/governance/) · [Routines](https://vstorm-co.github.io/agenticos/triggers/) ### 👥 Organize teams with roles and groups **Roles define what people may do. Groups define who you share with.** Use roles such as Builder, Operator, Member and Viewer, then create departments or working groups such as Operations, Engineering, Finance and Research. Share an agent, skill, collection, context file or app with a group in one step, or limit it to chosen departments when you create it. [Departments and groups](https://vstorm-co.github.io/agenticos/departments/) Bring existing company accounts through **OIDC single sign-on** (Entra ID, Okta, Keycloak and others), **LDAP directory login** or **Kerberos integrated Windows sign-in**. **Directory mappings** connect directory groups to a role and a group at sign-in. [Roles and permissions](https://vstorm-co.github.io/agenticos/permissions/) · [Directory sign-in](https://vstorm-co.github.io/agenticos/directory/) ## 🧭 Find your path Building on it? Reviewing security: data flows, identity, controls, what stays with your IT
Security is layered. Credentials sit in an envelope-encrypted vault. Code runs in isolated sandboxes. Published pages are sandboxed. Every organisation has a hash-chained audit log. Sessions are short-lived and revocable, and rate limits apply. Logs are redacted and data is swept on a retention schedule. | Outbound destination | Used when | Local alternative | |---|---|---| | Model provider | Every agent run | Ollama, vLLM or LM Studio on your hardware | | Embedding provider | Indexing and searching documents | Local Ollama embedding models | | LlamaParse | Collections set to that parser | PyMuPDF or LiteParse, both local | | Web search | Agents with web search enabled | Turn the capability off | | MCP servers, chat channels | Only those you connect | Self-hosted servers, web chat | | Logfire tracing | Only when a token is configured | Built-in run history | - **Vault:** a data key per secret, wrapped per organization and key version; master keys rotate; values are never shown again. - **Sandboxes:** the API holds no Docker socket; containers get no network unless needed, with CPU, process and time limits; gVisor optional. - **Audit log:** hash-chained per organization, verifiable and exportable. - **HIPAA profile:** [`deploy/profiles/hipaa/`](deploy/profiles/hipaa/) and `agenticos cmd doctor --profile hipaa` check a running deployment against the §164.312 technical safeguards. It is a configuration check, not a certification. [What it does not claim](https://vstorm-co.github.io/agenticos/security/#the-hipaa-profile-and-what-it-does-not-claim) - **Stays with your IT:** disk encryption at rest, egress firewall, MFA through your identity provider (no native MFA, SAML or SCIM), and backups that include the vault key. AgenticOS is the one you run yourself, on any model, with the source open. [Every comparison, in detail](https://vstorm-co.github.io/agenticos/about/comparison/). ## 🎯 Is AgenticOS the right fit? Choose it when a team has repeated document or tool-based work, subject experts who can maintain the instructions, and someone responsible for operating a self-hosted deployment. Know where it stops today: Source-system permissions are not mirrored automatically; an agent can lend its bound knowledge to its users. Self-hosting also requires an operator, and model quality, tool configuration and workload determine results. Read the current [limits and tradeoffs](https://vstorm-co.github.io/agenticos/about/comparison/#what-agenticos-does-not-do-yet). ## 🔐 Own your deployment, models and access **Sovereign means control over deployment, model providers, data flows and agent access.** AgenticOS is Apache-2.0 software you can inspect, modify and operate. There are two common setups. **Self-hosted, with hosted models:** AgenticOS, documents, vectors and logs run on your servers, and models come from a provider under your own contract and keys. **Fully local:** the same layer with open models through Ollama or vLLM on your hardware, plus local parsers and tools. Self-hosting the console does not make every model, parser or tool local, so review each destination you configure. Is AgenticOS free for commercial use? Yes. AgenticOS is licensed under Apache-2.0, which allows commercial use, modification and private deployment. You pay for the infrastructure you run it on and for the model providers and external services you choose. The AgenticOS name and logo are not covered by the licence.
Can AgenticOS run with local models only? Yes. Configure Ollama, LiteLLM or an OpenAI-compatible server such as vLLM or LM Studio as the model provider, use local embedding models through Ollama, and parse documents with PyMuPDF or LiteParse. Self-hosting the console alone does not make every model, parser or tool local: check each destination you configure. [Models](https://vstorm-co.github.io/agenticos/models/) · [Data flows](https://vstorm-co.github.io/agenticos/security/)
Which sign-in methods and roles does it support? Email and password with magic links, Google, generic OIDC single sign-on (Entra ID, Okta, Keycloak, Auth0, Authentik, Google Workspace), LDAP and Kerberos. Six built-in roles (Owner, Admin, Builder, Operator, Member, Viewer) combine with department groups and per-resource sharing. Multi-factor authentication comes from your identity provider; there is no native MFA, SAML or SCIM yet. [Permissions](https://vstorm-co.github.io/agenticos/permissions/)
How does AgenticOS keep agents under control? Monthly budgets per agent and per organisation are checked before each model request. Sensitive tools wait for a person's approval. Optional guardrails redact secrets and personal data, and every run is recorded with its agent version, tools, tokens and cost. [Governance](https://vstorm-co.github.io/agenticos/governance/)
How is it different from ChatGPT Enterprise, Copilot Studio or n8n? AgenticOS runs on your infrastructure with any of 28 model providers and has no seat or credit fee of its own. It builds agents for the organisation, published to chat, websites and APIs, rather than assistant seats for individual employees. Compared with n8n it starts from the agent rather than a workflow canvas, and many teams use both. The guides also cover the self-hosted builder [Dify](https://vstorm-co.github.io/agenticos/about/dify/) and coding agents such as Claude Code. [Comparisons](https://vstorm-co.github.io/agenticos/about/comparison/)
What does it take to run? Docker Compose on one host. A machine with 4 vCPU and 8 GB of RAM runs it, and two API workers suit a team of ten. Someone needs to own updates, backups (including the vault key), access and the external services you connect.
